page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU based on the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 8.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Storage is bundled as a 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps. The instance contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread efficiency paired with the expected throughput boundaries of a single core. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1741.0 and a multi-core score of 1736.0, showing performance parity across single- and multi-core suites due to the single vCPU configuration. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performed strongly at 14.0 GB/sec, while gzip compression reached 30.04 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded stress testing and total throughput tests such as PassMark CPU (986.83) and static web serving (2.38 GB/sec) scored in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth registered 30.06 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 11.68 GB/sec for large block writes.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency perspective, r8gd.medium provides access to Graviton-generation memory density and high-speed local NVMe storage at a minimal resource commitment. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of parallel core execution, making it unsuited for concurrent multi-threaded workloads or heavy computational compilation. It is well-fitted for lightweight caching layers, development and testing environments, Redis instances with moderate key counts, single-threaded data transformation jobs, and auxiliary database read replicas requiring rapid local scratch space.

It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, and includes a bundled 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded compute performance, scoring 1741.0 in Geekbench single-core and achieving 14.0 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Due to its single physical core constraint, aggregate multi-threaded throughput and parallel database operations remain limited. Economically advantageous for tasks with modest CPU requirements but elevated RAM and fast local storage demands, the r8gd.medium is appropriate for lightweight in-memory databases, development environments, staging caches, and low-concurrency data transformation tasks.
